principles: Only Authority config paths may consume the trust file; ordinary CLI behavior stays unchanged.
Explicit CLI/env configuration must always win over default local files.
Secret/trust material is local runtime input, never committed evidence.
Connection readiness is not Authority completion; receipt-backed proof remains mandatory.
drivers: User needs a default Authority Server trust profile without re-exporting variables every time.
The provided file uses LIVE_* alias names that current config code does not fully consume.
This area is security- and lifecycle-gate-sensitive, so overclaim prevention matters more than convenience.

options.name: A: Authority-scoped root authority_trust.env loader
pros: Solves the user-visible setup problem directly
Keeps file loading inside existing Authority config I/O shell
Allows alias mapping while preserving existing precedence and fail-closed semantics
cons: Requires targeted tests for precedence and off-mode zero-overclaim behavior

options.name: B: Ask users to manually export all variables
cons: Does not satisfy the request for default root-file use
Leaves repeated Authority setup fragile and easy to forget

options.name: C: Add generic dotenv loading for all CLI commands
pros: Broad convenience for future env files
cons: Arbitrary optimization beyond the real issue
Could leak unrelated env behavior into non-Authority commands
Harder to preserve host-neutral and fail-closed Authority boundaries

rationale: A fixes the real setup mismatch while keeping the change narrowly bounded to Authority config resolution and maintaining explicit env/CLI precedence.

preMortem.scenario: Default trust file overrides an explicitly exported production URL or key path.
preMortem.trigger: Loader merges file values after process.env instead of before.
preMortem.consequence: A caller may unknowingly connect to the wrong Authority profile.
preMortem.mitigation: Merge trust-file values only when canonical/legacy env keys are absent; add precedence smoke assertions.

preMortem.scenario: Root trust file makes off mode look Authority-ready.
preMortem.trigger: authority_status without authorityMode=enforce loads the trust file and reports configured readiness.
preMortem.consequence: Local workflow could be confused with Authority-backed workflow.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep off mode no-file/no-network semantics in loadAuthorityConfig; test off-mode no file read.

preMortem.scenario: Config readiness is misreported as production completion.
preMortem.trigger: Status output uses configured URL/key to set receiptVerified or productionDone.
preMortem.consequence: Lattice violates Authority receipt-backed completion semantics.
preMortem.mitigation: Assert receiptVerified/productionDone/canClaimProductionDone remain false without a verified receipt.
